positions.name: GateAsMandate
positions.frame: Is the Meridian signing gate — its requirement, its scope, and its ownership — being stated as a binding mandate enacted under authority, rather than offered as optional guidance or a proposal open to negotiation?
positions.why: Across relational, power, and conviction reads these four segments cohere as one authority-enactment: relational marks all four authority-ranking (the mint spans exactly src-1, src-3, src-4, src-5), power marks all four legitimate (formal process authority) rather than rational-persuasion, and conviction marks all four decision (settled, ratified) rather than claim (argued-for). The set holds a form-level tension worth naming rather than resolving: src-1 renders the mandate as flowing prose declarative ('now requires... before it ships') while src-3/src-4/src-5 render the same directional stance as clipped bolded header fragments (Gate/Scope/Owner) — different surface cadence, same enacted-authority read underneath.
